# Every setting and its default

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_variable_reference.py from roles/*/defaults/main.yml. Do not edit by hand:
     change the comment in the role's defaults file and run the script. -->

This page lists **every setting a role reads**, with the value it has when you set nothing, and
what the role's own comment says. It is generated from `roles/<role>/defaults/main.yml`, so it is
never out of date. Where to put a setting, and which place wins when it is in two, is in
[VARIABLES.md](VARIABLES.md). Values are shortened to one line here: the role file has the full one.

A setting that is a list (`[a, b]`) **replaces** the default list when you set it; it does not add
to it. Repeat the entries you want to keep.

**Contents:** [check_accounts](#check_accounts), [check_auditd](#check_auditd), [check_certs](#check_certs), [check_containers](#check_containers), [check_disk](#check_disk), [check_fapolicyd](#check_fapolicyd), [check_logging](#check_logging), [check_mariadb](#check_mariadb), [check_mounts](#check_mounts), [check_network](#check_network), [check_patching](#check_patching), [check_performance](#check_performance), [check_selinux](#check_selinux), [check_services](#check_services), [check_time](#check_time), [patch](#patch), [poam](#poam), [podman_discover](#podman_discover), [service_watch](#service_watch), [servicenow](#servicenow), [site_act](#site_act), [site_email](#site_email), [site_findings](#site_findings), [stigman_stack](#stigman_stack), [troubleshoot](#troubleshoot), [vmware_vm](#vmware_vm), [win_act](#win_act), [win_check_accounts](#win_check_accounts), [win_check_audit](#win_check_audit), [win_check_certs](#win_check_certs), [win_check_disk](#win_check_disk), [win_check_eventlog](#win_check_eventlog), [win_check_network](#win_check_network), [win_check_patching](#win_check_patching), [win_check_performance](#win_check_performance), [win_check_security](#win_check_security), [win_check_services](#win_check_services), [win_check_time](#win_check_time), [win_patch](#win_patch), [win_troubleshoot](#win_troubleshoot)

## check_accounts

File: `roles/check_accounts/defaults/main.yml`

> ACCOUNTS: the account problems auditors and attackers both look for, plus the one that quietly breaks automation - a service account password about to expire.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_accounts_min_uid` | `1000` | people's accounts start here |
| `check_accounts_inactive_days` | `35` | the STIG wants unused accounts disabled after 35 days |
| `check_accounts_ignore_inactive` | `[]` | Accounts that may stay unused (break-glass, service accounts that never log in interactively) |
| `check_accounts_nopasswd_allowed` | `[]` | sudoers entries allowed to use NOPASSWD, e.g. the account AAP connects as: [svc_aap, "%wheel"] |
| `check_accounts_expiry_watch` | `[]` | Accounts whose password/account expiry matters - above all the account AAP logs in with. e.g. [svc_aap] |
| `check_accounts_expiry_warn_days` | `14` |  |

## check_auditd

File: `roles/check_auditd/defaults/main.yml`

> AUDITD: the audit system records who did what (the STIG depends on it). Running, enabled in the kernel, rules loaded, no events lost, room for its log, and (optionally) forwarding. Also how MUCH it records: too much rotates the evidence away within hours, fills the disk (then auditd stops the host or puts it in single-user mode, as the STIG sets it up), drops records on the way to the SIEM, and uses up the SIEM licence.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_auditd_min_rules` | `5` | fewer loaded rules than this = the STIG rules are missing |
| `check_auditd_log_warn_pct` | `75` | the audit log's filesystem |
| `check_auditd_log_crit_pct` | `90` |  |
| `check_auditd_remote_required` | `false` | true = au-remote (audisp-remote) must be active |
| `check_auditd_exclude_accounts` | `[]` | Accounts whose audit events are expected in bulk and do NOT count toward the volume warning, e.g. the account a vulnerability scanner logs in with (a credentialed scan runs thousands of commands with sudo). Names or UIDs; a host that does not have the account skips it. The report still says how much they made, and the… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_auditd_volume_hours` | `24` | look at the audit records of the last N hours |
| `check_auditd_volume_warn_mb_day` | `200` | warning above this many MB of audit records a day (excluded accounts not counted) |
| `check_auditd_retention_warn_hours` | `24` | With max_log_file_action ROTATE, auditd keeps num_logs files of max_log_file MB and deletes the oldest. Warning when what is left on disk reaches back fewer hours than this. The STIG wants a week (168) when the records are NOT sent off the host as they are written (RHEL-08-030660). 0 = off. |
| `check_auditd_volume_timeout` | `120` | The breakdown (which account, which rule, which program) reads the audit log files of the window at low CPU and disk priority, and only when the volume or the retention is over its limit. It stops after this many seconds on a host with very large logs (and says so). |

File: `roles/check_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> CERTS: certificates that expire soon - as files on the host, inside Java keystores, and as served by TLS endpoints (what a browser or client actually sees).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|

| `check_certs_crit_days` | `14` |  |
| `check_certs_files` | `[]` | Certificate files (PEM) to check. Globs work. Every certificate in a file is checked (a chain file with an expiring intermediate is a problem too). e.g. [/etc/stigman/*.crt, /etc/pki/tls/certs/server.crt] |
| `check_certs_discover` | `true` | Also look for certificates in the usual places. Files with many certificates are CA bundles (hundreds of roots, noisy) and are skipped unless listed in check_certs_files. |
| `check_certs_discover_dirs` | `[/etc/pki/tls/certs, /etc/pki/nginx, /etc/nginx, /etc/httpd/conf.d, /etc/stigman]` |  |
| `check_certs_discover_exclude` | `'ca-bundle\|ca-certificates\|/localhost\.crt$'` |  |
| `check_certs_discover_max_per_file` | `10` |  |
| `check_certs_endpoints` | `[]` | TLS endpoints, checked FROM this host, e.g. the site's own web server: check_certs_endpoints: - {name: STIG Manager, host: 127.0.0.1, port: 443, servername: stigman.example.mil} |
| `check_certs_keystores` | `[]` | Java keystores (Tomcat, the ServiceNow MID Server ...). A JKS keystore lists without a password; a PKCS12 one needs it - give the NAME of an environment variable that holds it (set by an AAP credential), never the password itself: check_certs_keystores: - {path: /opt/servicenow/mid/agent/security/agent_keystore, passw… (all of it: the role file) |

## check_containers

File: `roles/check_containers/defaults/main.yml`

> CONTAINERS: the podman containers on the host - root's (rootful) and every user's (rootless) - found by themselves (roles/podman_discover: which ones exist, which systemd unit runs each one, which should be running). Read-only. Which containers and users are looked at, and which are left out: the podman_discover_* settings.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_containers_required` | `[]` | Containers that MUST exist and run on these hosts: a container name, or OWNER/NAME for one owner (root/web, alice/web). A name alone matches that container of any owner. Also matches a Quadlet file name without .container, e.g. [stigman-mysql, stigman-api, alice/web]. |
| `check_containers_recent_hours` | `24` | A container that stopped with an error (exit code not 0) this many hours ago or less is reported (containers:crashed). Older crashes are history and are not reported. |
| `check_containers_restart_warn` | `3` | More restarts than this (podman's restart count, or its systemd unit's) = a restart loop. |

## check_disk

File: `roles/check_disk/defaults/main.yml`

> DISK: how full each LOCAL filesystem is (space and inodes), and - from the history of earlier runs - how many days until it is full. Network filesystems (NFS) are the mounts check's job: a hung NFS server can make `df` hang, so this check never touches them.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_disk_warn_pct` | `85` | % used -> warning |
| `check_disk_crit_pct` | `95` | % used -> critical |
| `check_disk_inode_warn_pct` | `85` | inodes: too many small files fill a disk too |
| `check_disk_inode_crit_pct` | `95` |  |
| `check_disk_overrides` | `{}` | Different limits for particular mount points, e.g. keep the audit log partition emptier: check_disk_overrides: /var/log/audit: {warn: 70, crit: 85} |
| `check_disk_ignore` | `- '^/(proc\|sys\|dev\|run)(/\|$)' - '^/etc/(hosts\|hostname\|resolv\.conf)$' # bind-mounted fil…` | Mount points to skip (regular expressions). |
| `check_disk_exclude_types` | `[tmpfs, devtmpfs, squashfs, overlay, iso9660, efivarfs, nsfs]` |  |
| `check_disk_forecast` | `true` | Days-until-full forecast. Each run adds a sample (date, bytes used) per mount to a small file on the host; once there is at least a day of history, the growth rate predicts when the filesystem fills. Check mode (a dry run) reads the history but does not add to it. |
| `check_disk_forecast_warn_days` | `14` |  |
| `check_disk_forecast_crit_days` | `3` |  |
| `check_disk_history_file` | `/var/lib/site-health/disk-history.json` |  |
| `check_disk_history_keep_days` | `30` |  |
| `check_disk_timeout` | `20` | seconds for df |

File: `roles/check_fapolicyd/defaults/main.yml`

> FAPOLICYD (application allow-listing): running, enforcing, configuration and trust database valid, and recent denials - which is what you see when it blocks a program.

| `check_fapolicyd_denials_warn` | `1` |  |

## check_mounts

File: `roles/check_mounts/defaults/main.yml`

> MOUNTS: filesystems that should be mounted but are not, local filesystems that went read-only (the kernel does that after disk errors), and network mounts (NFS/CIFS) that hang. Diagnose only: this check never mounts, unmounts or remounts anything.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_mounts_network_types` | `[nfs, nfs4, cifs, smb3]` |  |
| `check_mounts_local_types` | `[xfs, ext4, ext3, btrfs, vfat]` |  |
| `check_mounts_timeout` | `5` | seconds before a network mount counts as hung |
| `check_mounts_warn_pct` | `85` | Network mounts: how full (same idea as the disk check) |
| `check_mounts_crit_pct` | `95` |  |
| `check_mounts_ignore` | `[]` | fstab mount points that are allowed to be unmounted (regular expressions) |

|---|---|---|

| `check_network_resolve_self` | `true` | this host's own full name (hostname -f) resolves |
| `check_network_dns_names` | `[]` | e.g. [ldap.example.mil, servicenow.example.mil] |
| `check_network_tcp` | `[]` | TCP services this host needs, e.g. check_network_tcp: - {name: LDAP, host: ldap.example.mil, port: 636} - {name: SIEM (syslog over TLS), host: siem.example.mil, port: 6514} |
| `check_network_timeout` | `5` |  |

## check_selinux

File: `roles/check_selinux/defaults/main.yml`

> SELINUX: enforcing (the STIG requires it), the config file agrees (so a reboot does not change it), no locally added permissive domains, and recent denials (AVCs) - which is what you see when SELinux blocks an application.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_selinux_expected_mode` | `enforcing` |  |
| `check_selinux_avc_since` | `yesterday` | ausearch -ts: recent (10 min), today, yesterday, this-week |
| `check_selinux_avc_warn` | `1` | this many denials or more -> warning |
| `check_selinux_booleans` | `{}` | Booleans that must have a value, e.g. {httpd_can_network_connect: "on"} |
| `check_selinux_relabel_paths` | `[]` | Paths whose file labels are compared with the policy (a dry-run restorecon). Mislabeled files are a common cause of denials after files are copied or moved. Keep it to small trees. e.g. [/etc/nginx, /var/www, /etc/stigman] |

| `patch_never_reboot_groups` | `[aap, aap_hosts, sat, netapp, netapp_console_hosts]` | Hosts in these groups are patched but NEVER rebooted by this playbook (reboot them by hand, in a maintenance window). Add your own group names; the built-in protection below is on always. |
| `patch_never_patch_groups` | `[no_patch, aap, aap_hosts, sat, netapp, netapp_console_hosts]` | Hosts in these groups are skipped entirely (Satellite is upgraded with satellite-maintain, not dnf). |
| `patch_min_free_mb` | `1024` | BUILT IN, whatever you set above (roles/patch/vars/main.yml): the AAP hosts (groups aap and aap_hosts) are never patched and never rebooted by a job, and neither is the machine the job runs from (a local connection). A package script can restart services under the running job. Set the two lists above only to ADD group… (all of it: the role file) |
| `patch_service_wait` | `120` | seconds to wait for services to come back after a reboot |
| `patch_ignore_services` | `'^(user@\|user-runtime-dir@\|session-\|dnf-makecache\|packagekit\|fwupd\|run-\|systemd-(hostname…` | Services that come and go on their own and are not compared before/after (regular expression) |

## podman_discover

File: `roles/podman_discover/defaults/main.yml`

> PODMAN DISCOVERY (read-only): every podman container on the host, root's (rootful) and each user's (rootless), with how it is run (a systemd unit or plain podman) and whether it should be running. Used by the Health check `containers` and by Service watch. It changes nothing.

## servicenow

File: `roles/servicenow/defaults/main.yml`

> SERVICENOW - open, update (and optionally resolve) incidents from check findings, and check that ServiceNow itself (the instance and its MID Servers) is healthy. Uses the REST Table API with ansible.builtin.uri: no extra collection to install. Connection: the "ServiceNow API" AAP credential sets SN_HOST (https://<instance>), SN_USERNAME and SN_PASSWORD in the job's environment. Without it, nothing is sent: the job prints what it WOULD have opened (a safe way to try it out).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `servicenow_min_severity` | `warning` | Findings at or above this severity get a ticket: critical \| warning |
| `servicenow_table` | `incident` |  |
| `servicenow_assignment_group` | (empty) | Values for new incidents. Names work (the API is asked to accept display values), e.g. servicenow_assignment_group: Linux Operations |
| `servicenow_caller` | (empty) | user name; empty = the API account |
| `servicenow_category` | (empty) | e.g. Software |
| `servicenow_urgency` | `{critical: "1", warning: "2"}` |  |
| `servicenow_impact` | `{critical: "2", warning: "3"}` |  |
| `servicenow_set_ci` | `true` | set Configuration item = the host name (must exist in the CMDB) |
| `servicenow_note_cleared` | `true` | When a problem that had a ticket is gone, add a work note (and, if you want, resolve it). |
| `servicenow_resolve_cleared` | `false` |  |
| `servicenow_resolved_state` | `"6"` | Resolved |
| `servicenow_close_code` | `"Solution provided"` | must be a close code your instance has |
| `servicenow_note_repeats` | `true` | Add a work note to an open ticket each time its finding is seen again. |
| `servicenow_correlation_prefix` | `site-health` | Every ticket from these playbooks carries a correlation ID starting with this, so the same problem on the same host always updates the same ticket. |
| `servicenow_validate_certs` | `true` |  |
| `servicenow_ca_path` | (empty) | A CA bundle (PEM) for the instance's TLS certificate, when the execution environment does not trust its CA (e.g. a DoD root CA): a path on the controller, such as a file you add to the project: servicenow_ca_path: "{{ playbook_dir }}/files/ca/servicenow-ca.pem". Empty = the execution environment's normal trust store.… (all of it: the role file) |
| `servicenow_timeout` | `30` |  |
| `servicenow_fail_when_findings` | `true` | Fail the job when it opened/updated tickets, so the workflow shows red while problems exist. |
| `servicenow_check_mid` | `true` | servicenow_health.yml: also check the MID Servers (needs read access to the ecc_agent table) |
| `servicenow_slow_seconds` | `5` | the API answering slower than this -> warning |
| `servicenow_test_resolve` | `true` | servicenow_test_ticket.yml: resolve the test incident at the end (false = leave it open to look at) |

## site_email

File: `roles/site_email/defaults/main.yml`

> EMAIL A REPORT through your mail relay (SMTP). Off until report_email_to has an address. Used by every report job: health checks, certificate reports, database health, POA&M, ServiceNow health, troubleshooting, the VMware jobs (docs/EMAIL_REPORTS.md). The relay settings belong in playbooks/group_vars/all.yml. If the relay needs a login, attach an "SMTP relay" credential (aap/credential_types/smtp_relay.yml) - never put a password in these settings.

| `report_email_html_template` | `report.html.j2` | The look of the HTML version. Your own: copy roles/site_email/templates/report.html.j2 (e.g. to playbooks/files/email/report.html.j2), change it, and set report_email_html_template: "{{ playbook_dir }}/files/email/report.html.j2" |

## site_findings

File: `roles/site_findings/defaults/main.yml`

> Shared by every check playbook. A "finding" is one thing that is wrong on one host:   check:    the check that found it (disk, services, mariadb, ...)   id:       a stable name for this problem on this host, e.g. disk:/var. ServiceNow uses it to             update the same ticket instead of opening a new one every run.   severity: critical \| warning   summary:  one line a person understands ("/var is 96% full (critical at 95%)")   hint:     a read-only command that shows more. A person can paste it into a shell; ACT (when             you add it later) runs it to collect evidence. Check roles only ADD findings. This role starts the list, reports it, and decides pass/fail.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `site_fail_on` | `[critical, warning]` | Which severities make the job FAIL. A failed job is what sends an AAP workflow down its "on failure" path (open tickets, ask ACT, wait for approval). [] = report only, never fail. |
| `site_syslog` | `true` | One syslog line per finding (tag below), so your log server / SIEM sees them too. |
| `site_syslog_tag` | `site-health` |  |
| `site_eventlog_source` | `site-health` | Windows: one Application event log entry per finding instead of syslog (source below). |
| `site_os` | `linux` | ---- Linux or Windows (set by the playbook; do not set) ----------------------------------------- Linux playbooks run the roles check_<name>, the Windows ones (win_*.yml) the roles win_check_<name>. |
| `site_check_role_prefix` | `"{{ 'win_check_' if site_os == 'windows' else 'check_' }}"` |  |
| `site_windows_connections` | `[winrm, psrp, ansible.builtin.winrm, ansible.builtin.psrp]` | How a host is recognized as Windows: its connection, or its shell (Windows OpenSSH). |
| `_site_host_is_windows` | (worked out by the role; see its file) |  |
| `site_settings_notice` | `true` | A notice in the job output when a project settings file (playbooks/group_vars/*.yml) defines a setting: it wins over AAP's inventory Variables box. false = no notice. |

File: `roles/win_check_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS CERTIFICATES: every certificate in the machine stores below, and which of them are in use (https bindings of IIS / WSUS / ..., the WinRM HTTPS listener AAP connects through, Remote Desktop). Expiring soon -> warning / critical. Expired: critical when in use, or when it expired less than win_check_certs_expired_report_days ago (older leftovers are only listed in the certificate report).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_certs_warn_days` | `30` |  |
| `win_check_certs_crit_days` | `7` |  |
| `win_check_certs_expired_report_days` | `30` |  |
| `win_check_certs_stores` | `['Cert:\LocalMachine\My', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\WebHosting', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Remote Des…` |  |
| `win_check_certs_ignore_subjects` | `[]` | wildcards, e.g. ['CN=localhost*'] |
| `win_check_certs_endpoints` | `[]` | TLS services whose certificate a client actually gets, e.g. win_check_certs_endpoints: - {name: IIS, host: 127.0.0.1, port: 443, servername: web01.yoursite.mil} |

## win_check_disk

File: `roles/win_check_disk/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS DISK: how full each local fixed volume (C:, D:, ...) is.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_disk_warn_pct` | `85` | % used -> warning |
| `win_check_disk_crit_pct` | `95` | % used -> critical |
| `win_check_disk_min_free_gb` | `0` | also warn below this many GiB free (0 = off): big volumes |
| `win_check_disk_overrides` | `{}` | Different limits for particular volumes, e.g. a database volume kept full on purpose: win_check_disk_overrides: 'D:': {warn: 92, crit: 98} |
| `win_check_disk_ignore` | `[]` | volumes not to check, e.g. ['E:'] |

## win_check_eventlog

File: `roles/win_check_eventlog/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS EVENT LOG, the last win_check_eventlog_hours:   - unexpected shutdown or power loss (41, 6008), a crash / blue screen (1001)  -> critical   - disk and file system errors (disk, Ntfs, storage drivers)                    -> critical   - the Security log was cleared (1102)                                           -> critical   - many errors in System + Application (the finding names the top sources)       -> warning   - a System / Application / Security log that is full and not overwriting        -> critical

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_eventlog_hours` | `24` |  |
| `win_check_eventlog_error_warn` | `50` |  |

## win_check_network

File: `roles/win_check_network/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS NETWORK, from the server itself:   - a default gateway and DNS servers are configured;   - the names you list resolve, the TCP services you list answer;   - domain members: the computer's trust with the domain works (nltest /sc_query). A broken     trust is the classic "the trust relationship between this workstation and the primary     domain failed" at logon.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_network_dns_names` | `[]` | Names every Windows server must resolve, e.g. [dc01.yoursite.mil, ldap.yoursite.mil] |
| `win_check_network_tcp` | `[]` | Services every Windows server must reach, e.g. win_check_network_tcp: - {name: LDAPS, host: dc01.yoursite.mil, port: 636} - {name: SIEM, host: siem.yoursite.mil, port: 9997} |
| `win_check_network_secure_channel` | `true` |  |
| `win_check_network_timeout_ms` | `3000` |  |

> WINDOWS PATCHING (read-only; installing updates is a later runbook)   - a restart is pending for installed updates (Windows Update, component servicing, ConfigMgr)   - days since the last update was installed (Get-HotFix)   - optional: ask Windows Update which updates are missing (slower; needs full PowerShell)

| `win_check_patching_reboot_pending` | `true` |  |
| `win_check_patching_search_pending` | `false` |  |

## win_check_security

File: `roles/win_check_security/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS SECURITY BASELINE (a few high-value STIG items; not a full STIG scan: that is your SCAP / vulnerability scanner)

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_security_av` | `auto` | Antivirus: auto = check Microsoft Defender when it is the active antivirus (skipped when it is passive or off because another product protects the server); defender = always; none = never. |
| `win_check_security_av_signature_max_days` | `7` |  |
| `win_check_security_av_services` | `[]` | Services of your endpoint protection that must run, e.g. Trellix / McAfee: [masvc, mfemms] |
| `win_check_security_firewall_profiles` | `[Domain, Private, Public]` | must be on |
| `win_check_security_smb1` | `true` | SMBv1 must be off |
| `win_check_security_rdp_nla` | `true` | Remote Desktop must require Network Level Authentication |
| `win_check_security_uac` | `true` | User Account Control must be on |
| `win_check_security_legacy_tls` | `true` | TLS 1.0 / 1.1 must be off for incoming connections |

## win_check_services

File: `roles/win_check_services/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS SERVICES   - every required service must be running (critical);   - an automatic service that stopped WITH AN ERROR (exit code not 0) is a warning. Automatic     services that stop cleanly by design (trigger-start, delayed) are not reported;   - a service that crashed several times recently (System log events 7031 / 7034).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_services_required` | `[EventLog, RpcSs, Dnscache, W32Time, WinRM, mpssvc]` | Must be running on every Windows server. Add your own per group with ..._required_extra, e.g. for IIS servers: win_check_services_required_extra: [W3SVC, WAS] |
| `win_check_services_required_extra` | `[]` |  |
| `win_check_services_ignore` | `- gupdate - gupdatem - edgeupdate - edgeupdatem - MicrosoftEdgeElevationService - GoogleU…` | Automatic services never to report (wildcards allowed: * and ?) |
| `win_check_services_crash_hours` | `24` | look back this far for unexpected stops |
| `win_check_services_crash_warn` | `3` | this many unexpected stops of one service -> warning |

## win_check_time

File: `roles/win_check_time/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS TIME: the Windows Time service runs, syncs with a real source (not the local clock), synced recently, and how far off the clock is from its source. Kerberos (domain logons) fails when a clock is 5 minutes off.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_time_offset_warn_sec` | `1` |  |
| `win_check_time_offset_crit_sec` | `5` |  |
| `win_check_time_max_hours_since_sync` | `24` |  |

## win_patch

File: `roles/win_patch/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS PATCH through the ConfigMgr client: install what Software Center has for the server (the software updates deployed to it), restart if the updates need it, and prove the server came back: every automatic service that was running before runs again. One server at a time by default; the rollout stops at the first server that fails. Check mode lists and changes nothing.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `automatic_restarts` | `false` | NO AUTOMATIC RESTARTS unless you say so: this playbook restarts a server only when automatic_restarts is true (the job template's Variables, or the survey) and the updates need it. With automatic_restarts false (the default) it installs the updates and tells you which servers still need a restart; a person restarts th… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_patch_never_reboot_groups` | `"{{ patch_never_reboot_groups \| default(['aap', 'aap_hosts', 'sat', 'netapp', 'netapp_con…` | Servers in these groups are patched but NEVER restarted by this playbook (restart them by hand). Follows the Linux setting (patch_never_reboot_groups) when you set it, so ONE list covers both; the fallback is the Linux role's default (roles/patch/defaults/main.yml; tests/test_protection.py checks it). |
| `win_patch_never_patch_groups` | `"{{ patch_never_patch_groups \| default(['no_patch', 'aap', 'aap_hosts', 'sat', 'netapp',…` | Servers in these groups are skipped entirely (e.g. servers patched only by hand). |
| `win_patch_scan_first` | `true` | ask the client to rescan and re-evaluate before installing |
| `win_patch_scan_wait_sec` | `120` | let that scan settle |
| `win_patch_timeout_min` | `120` | per round: download + install |
| `win_patch_poll_sec` | `30` | how often to look at the progress |
| `win_patch_max_rounds` | `2` | After a restart, look again: servicing-stack and cumulative updates often reveal more updates. |
| `win_patch_restart_delay_sec` | `30` | shutdown.exe /t |
| `win_patch_restart_timeout_min` | `30` | how long the server may take to come back |
| `win_patch_restart_settle_sec` | `30` | after the port answers again, before trying to log on |
| `win_patch_reconnect_pause_sec` | `20` | between logon attempts after the restart |
| `win_patch_services_grace_min` | `5` | After the restart, give delayed-start services this long before calling one missing. |
| `win_patch_services_ignore` | `['gupdate*', 'edgeupdate*', 'MicrosoftEdgeElevationService', 'GoogleUpdater*', 'MapsBroke…` | Automatic services that come and go on their own (wildcards); not compared before/after. |
| `win_patch_winrm_host` | `"{{ ansible_host \| default(inventory_hostname) }}"` | Where AAP reaches WinRM, to see the server go down and come back during the restart |
| `win_patch_winrm_port` | `"{{ ansible_port \| default(5986) }}"` |  |
